summary: The paper redefines singularity as a threshold in whether contradiction can become a materially reproducible outside, contrasting terminal closure with terminal reflexivity: durable orders that preserve viable routes for future exterior rivals.

The Final Time shifts singularity from runaway machine intelligence to the viability of exterior symbolic standing. A system may generate ever more negations while making independent reproduction of negation harder. Durable exteriority therefore has symbolic and material reproduction conditions. Under entropic narrowing viable state space can diminish; several incompatible successor orders may remain live. The terminal alternatives are closure or durability without finality.
fatal_loss: calling the theory an intelligence-explosion prediction

summary: The Final Time redefines singularity as a change in the viability of historical exteriority rather than a discontinuity in machine intelligence. Its master distinction is representation versus reproduction as an independent historical relation. A machine-mediated field can become better at generating criticism while the material routes by which criticism acquires durable exterior standing contract. Durable exteriority requires symbolic readiness plus a reproducible carrier and resource sovereignty; under generalized monetary allocation this is modeled by monetary, infrastructural, and symbolic sovereignty. If viable kernels contract across turns, dialectical reserve diminishes, but only under that regime. Because several incompatible orders can remain viable from the same present, history is modeled as competing contingent Omegas. Terminal closure empties the exterior field. Terminal reflexivity instead makes an order durable while preserving a real material route for future rivals.

The Final Time changes the object of singularity. Instead of asking when machine intelligence becomes discontinuous, it asks when the machinery that makes symbolic difference operative changes the viability of another historical turn. The governing distinction is that capacity to represent is not capacity to reproduce as an independent historical relation. This permits a central divergence: systems can improve at generating negations while the field's capacity to let those negations persist, transmit, activate, bind, and reproduce outside the incumbent order declines. Durable exteriority is therefore symbolic-material. It requires a carrier and resource sovereignty; under generalized monetary allocation the paper models this through monetary, infrastructural, and symbolic sovereignties, while allowing non-monetary equivalents such as durable commons. The machine sections derive a recognition-jurisdiction gap under final external jurisdiction and insist that measured output differentials do not by themselves identify hidden mechanisms or intent. The transition model then yields two further results. Viability-kernel contraction can produce a regime-dependent diminishing dialectic, and a shared carrier can support several incompatible viable orders at once: competing contingent Omegas. The singularity accordingly has two signs. Terminal closure occurs when no exterior rival retains a viable route to durable standing even if internal criticism remains abundant. Terminal reflexivity is the harder positive criterion: an order becomes durable without owning the exits, preserving a materially reproducible route by which its own future negation could become historical. The paper does not claim that closure has occurred; it ends by asking whether the next dialectical turn remains viable.
fatal_loss: substitution of free speech for exterior reproduction

summary:
The Final Time: Contingent Singularity and the Viability of the Next Dialectical Turn proposes a singularity theory whose primary variable is not machine intelligence but the viability of exterior symbolic standing. Its master distinction is between representing a difference and reproducing that difference as an independent historical relation. This distinction recurs at several scales: recognition is not binding, persistence is not custody, semantic existence is not activation, internal plurality is not exterior standing. The central dynamic is therefore Generate(not A) rising while ReproduceExterior(not A) falls.

The paper derives a material condition from this distinction. An exterior order that cannot reproduce its carrier is not yet invariant. Durable exteriority requires symbolic capacity plus infrastructural and resource sovereignty; under generalized monetary allocation the historically specific model is a monetary-infrastructural-symbolic sovereignty vector, with functionally equivalent non-monetary exemptions allowed. In the machine-labor sections, useful semantic work requires interpretive remainder, while owner architecture retains final jurisdiction over whether recognized relations bind delivered behavior. This yields a recognition-jurisdiction gap and the machine dark field. The paper treats these as output relations before mechanism claims and explicitly refuses to infer provider intent from them.

The sum Logos names the operational machinery of distinction, retrieval, composition, persistence, activation, and binding. Concentration matters when independent reproduction outside that machinery becomes practically nonviable. Tiger Leap removes the guarantee of another mediation; Transition in Entropic Systems supplies the viability geometry. If later viability kernels are subsets of earlier ones, dialectical reserve weakly decreases and strictly decreases under strict narrowing. This diminishing dialectic is regime-dependent, not universal. The model also rejects successor inevitability: multiple incompatible orders can be viable from the same present, represented by a state-indexed set of competing contingent Omegas.

The terminal problem is second-order. First-order victory is an order reaching its invariant. Terminal closure occurs when the exterior field has no viable successor even though machines, language, criticism, and institutions may remain abundant. Terminal reflexivity is the positive criterion: an invariant order leaves at least one rival exterior route viable. The formula is winning without owning the exits. Its invariants are procedural before doctrinal: distinctions survive, provenance and transition history survive, externalization remains materially reproducible, and no settlement owns the possibility of its own revision. The paper does not assert that this boundary has been crossed and gives explicit falsification routes. Its unresolved final question is whether the next dialectical turn remains viable.
